definition: Pyramid, or pyramid representation, is a type of multi-scale signal representation developed by the computer vision, image processing and signal processing communities, in which a signal or an image is subject to repeated smoothing and subsampling.
details: Pyramid representation is a predecessor to scale-space representation and multiresolution analysis.

explainer.lead: A pyramid is a multi-scale image representation where the image is repeatedly smoothed and subsampled. It matters because it lets algorithms analyze structure at multiple resolutions efficiently.

tiers.eli5: It's the same picture saved at several sizes, from full detail down to tiny, so you can look at big shapes or fine detail.
tiers.practitioner: Used to build multi-scale features for detection and matching; the pitfall is losing fine detail at coarse levels, so results depend on the level chosen.
tiers.paperLevel: A multi-scale signal representation produced by repeated smoothing and subsampling; it is a predecessor to scale-space representation and multiresolution analysis.

explainer.example: An image is smoothed and subsampled repeatedly to form a stack of progressively smaller versions.
